Affiliation:: Department of Psychology, University of Oklahoma
Application Areas: Adolescent Social Development and Peer Dynamics
Disaster Resilience and Structural Safety Engineering
LGBTQ+ Mental Health and Digital Identity Support
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Social Status Differentiation: Distinguishing between social acceptance and prestige/power to understand developmental shifts in peer hierarchies and gender norm conformity (e.g., Peer Nomination, Vignette Rating, and Hierarchical Regression Analysis of adolescent cohorts).

Multimodal Disaster Reconstruction: Integrating forensic structural engineering data with qualitative survivor narratives to evaluate human-environment interactions and sheltering decisions during extreme weather events (e.g., StEER Protocols, UASs, and Semistructured Survivor Interviews).

Contextual Risk and Resilience Modeling: Applying hierarchical regression and thematic analysis to examine how diverse social support systems (online vs. offline) moderate psychological adjustment and mitigate internalized stigma in marginalized populations (e.g., Transgender Young Adult Cohort and Online Community Forums).
Summary Description: Lara Mayeux is a developmental psychologist at the University of Oklahoma specializing in adolescent peer dynamics, disaster sociology, and LGBTQ+ mental health. Her research distinguishes peer acceptance from social power, utilizing experimental priming and peer nominations to analyze gender prototypicality and status hierarchies. Mayeux uniquely bridges psychology and forensic engineering, combining structural assessments with survivor narratives to evaluate tornado survivability and sheltering efficacy. Most recently, she applies risk and resilience frameworks to transgender young adults, examining how digital and offline social support mitigate internalized transphobia. Her work consistently highlights how social contexts and environmental factors shape human resilience and identity development across diverse populations.
